title: Quantum Advantage for Distributed Symmetry Breaking
authors: Maxime Flin, Longcheng Li, Jukka Suomela
abstract: We present a distributed quantum algorithm that $3$-colors cycles in $O(1)$ rounds, with high probability. It follows that all locally checkable labeling problems (LCLs) that have round complexity $O(\log^* n)$ in the classical LOCAL model can be solved in $O(1)$ rounds in the quantum-LOCAL model, with high probability; this includes problems such as maximal independent set and maximal matching in bounded-degree graphs. This presents the first natural examples of graph problems with an asymptotic distributed quantum advantage for the LOCAL model; all prior examples that separate LOCAL and quantum-LOCAL are artificial problems constructed merely for the sake of demonstrating quantum advantage.
summary: This work presents a quantum algorithm achieving a significant speedup for solving graph problems like coloring and finding independent sets in the distributed quantum setting. By showing that certain problems solvable in polylogarithmic classical rounds can be solved in constant quantum rounds, it establishes the first natural examples of quantum advantage for the LOCAL model. The methodology involves advanced quantum information theory applied to graph structures.
main_problem: The paper aims to demonstrate and quantify the quantum advantage for solving natural graph problems in the distributed computing setting, specifically within the LOCAL model.
main_result: It shows that any Locally Checkable Labeling Problem (LCL) solvable in $O(\log^* n)$ rounds classically can be solved in $O(1)$ rounds quantum-locally, providing natural examples of quantum advantage.
method: The authors develop quantum algorithms by constructing specific one-way quantum-LOCAL operators and analyzing their convergence properties using operator norms and energy bounds.
model_or_system: The theoretical framework is the comparison between the classical LOCAL model and the quantum-LOCAL model for distributed computation on input graphs. The core mechanism involves analyzing the time evolution of quantum operators related to graph colorings.
key_observables: Round complexity (e.g., $O(1)$ vs. $\Theta(\log^* n)$), local failure probability ($\le \epsilon$), and the expectation values of time evolution operators $p_n(w)$.
important_parameters: The number of colors ($q$), the convergence parameter ($s$), and the maximum degree ($\Delta$) of the graph.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on bounding operator norms (Frobenius norm) and assuming the smallness of error terms ($\eta$) relative to the required precision.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing a core result (1-round quantum coloring of cycles) to generalizing this to all LCLs. The mathematical development involves constructing the necessary quantum operators via iterative methods and proving their convergence and positivity.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical techniques used to establish quantum advantage in a highly structured computational model like the LOCAL model are relevant for understanding the limits of quantum computation in distributed physical systems.
